papers.title: Batched Speech Decisions Without Decoding: Single-Token Supervision Lets a Frozen LLM Hear Beyond the Transcript
papers.problem: Voice agents answer small yes-or-no style questions by slow word-by-word decoding.
papers.fix: A frozen LLM reads each answer in one step, giving 80 decisions on eight utterances in about 0.1 seconds.
papers.practicalUseCase: Voice agents can react faster and also hear gender and emotion, so use single-token answers for closed decisions.
papers.limitation: Adding the voice-hearing connector cost 1 point of spoken question-answering accuracy, from 83% to 82%.

papers.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
papers.problem: Judges that check an agent's tool arguments reject correct values when no text in their input shows the source.
papers.fix: A second model writes a reference first, lifting judge accuracy on the controlled test to 98.40-99.59 AUROC.
papers.practicalUseCase: Your agent checker may fail correct default values, so give it a written reference for each value.
papers.limitation: The paper tests seven judges and three benchmarks, so other judges and tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Long-horizon Work Agents
papers.problem: Hand-built training worlds for work agents cost too much engineering, and auto-built worlds lose realism or checkable answers.
papers.fix: WorkForge built 16.7K checkable environments, and training on them raised one model's GDPVal score from 45.5 to 73.6.
papers.practicalUseCase: Agent training can scale if every task ties to facts in real files, so build checks from file content.
papers.limitation: The paper reports results on a few model families and benchmarks, so gains may differ elsewhere.

papers.title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation
papers.problem: Robot teams cannot easily tell which teammate or which reported object to trust without preset trust or side signals.
papers.fix: NeST-Bayes reached 98.8% robot precision and 93.8% recall under strong attacks, using only whether robots' observations agree.
papers.practicalUseCase: Robot teams can drop bad data from faulty or hostile robots, so check cross-robot agreement before you trust a report.
papers.limitation: Results come from benchmarks and one simulated warehouse, where robot recall fell to 92.0% and object recall to 85.0%.

papers.title: Sharīʿah Compliance in Malaysia’s Digital Payment Systems: Evidence from Expert Interviews
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.leadAuthor: Wan Anis Wan Mohd Assrudin et al.
papers.problem: Malaysia has rules for digital payments, but experts still doubt that non-bank payment providers follow Sharia in practice.
papers.fix: Ten Sharia experts named problems in daily operations, technology limits, returns, user awareness, and data security.
papers.practicalUseCase: Users of non-bank payment apps cannot assume Sharia compliance, so check who governs the provider first.
papers.limitation: The study covers only Malaysia and ten interviews, so it shows expert views, not measured compliance.

papers.title: Financial Depth and Stability in Dual Banking Systems
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: It was unclear whether mixing Islamic and conventional banking helps a country's economy grow.
papers.fix: Across 27 countries, a larger Islamic asset share raised private credit (beta 0.3725) and real output (beta 0.0842).
papers.practicalUseCase: Policymakers can back dual banking, and Islamic small-business credit lines look useful to fund.
papers.limitation: The model has no comparison with fully single-system countries, so it cannot show dual banking beats them.

papers.title: Financing Government Issuances via Service Ownership Ṣukūk
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Gulf governments face fiscal deficits and joblessness, and sovereign sukuk usually back physical assets, not labour.
papers.fix: In a Gulf model, labour-service sukuk cut the deficit by 1.5 GDP points and financing cost by 62 basis points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Sukuk could fund public jobs without interest, if the model holds in real economies.
papers.limitation: The model covers only Gulf economies and ignores differences between households, so poorer Muslim countries need further study.

papers.title: Interest Prohibitions and Contract Design in Medieval Christianity and Islam
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Historians lacked a clear link between interest bans and the credit contracts that people actually used.
papers.fix: Medieval Europe hid returns inside exchange terms, while Islamic law placed returns in trade and partnerships with clear risk sharing.
papers.practicalUseCase: Disputes over interest rules turn on contract form, so check ownership transfer, records, and who carries the loss.
papers.limitation: The study reads doctrine and secondary history, and it adds no new archive data or prevalence numbers.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and peer comparison, and nobody had pooled how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: A review of studies found impostor feelings were frequent among medical students before licensing.
papers.practicalUseCase: Feeling like a fraud is common among high-pressure trainees, so you are not alone and should not hide it.
papers.limitation: Results varied widely by sampling method and region, so the pooled estimate needs cautious reading.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: AI tools may help doctoral students innovate, but what actually drives their innovation was unclear.
papers.fix: Inner drive and outside rewards both raised innovation among chemistry doctoral students, and long unmet needs sharply lowered it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Keep your basic needs met, since a drained researcher stops exploring, and good resources only help a motivated one.
papers.limitation: The data are one-time self-reports from chemistry students, so they show links, not cause.
